solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stunning wine put into wrong glass at first

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, so the wine goes into the wrong-plus-letter pair

parts.note: a wrong is a sin
hock is a German white wine

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word glass is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone shockingly pours wine into the wrong glass to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stunning is startling or appalling, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Natural boundary providing advantage in hotel dispute

indicators.note: the advantage sits inside the hotel-plus-dispute pair

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
a row is a quarrel or dispute
an edge is an advantage, as in having the edge

explanation.surface: A hotel argument gives someone the upper hand over a neighbouring boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of bushes is a living, natural field boundary in the countryside.

clue.text: Communication cords?

parts.note: the train's emergency cord is suggested, but read as linked messages: letters forwarded in a chain

explanation.definitionFit: These are messages passed on person to person in a chain, so communications that form cords of links.

clue.text: One depends on freezing point

parts.note: depends means hangs down; something hanging that exists only at the freezing point

explanation.definitionFit: A tapering spike of ice hangs (depends) from a gutter, forming only around freezing temperature.

clue.text: Valley of angels flying without wings

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered into a new arrangement
wings are the outer letters, so the first and last letters of angels are dropped

explanation.surface: Angels flying over a valley with no wings at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without wings' leaves NGEL from angels, and 'flying' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Scottish word for a narrow valley, a straight synonym.

clue.text: A film is always vetted

definitions.meaning: every film is shown in cinemas, put up on the big picture
vetted means checked over or examined before approval

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition completes a sentence: a film is always shown on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is shown in cinemas, and a candidate who is vetted has been checked out.

clue.text: Partners welcome a good salary

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the partners enclose the next letters

parts.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A couple welcome a decent salary.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge the players sit as pairs, North-South and East-West, so 'Partners' can give W and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay for work is a wage, a close synonym of salary.

clue.text: Cast out — joint set for surgery

indicators.note: a joint set by surgery is rearranged, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An orthopaedic surgeon resets a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, so to cast out.

clue.text: Church by West Coast city to charge rent

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, on the American west coast
CE is the Church of England
to rate is to set a price or charge

explanation.surface: A church near Los Angeles intends to charge rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment for a home but is the verb to tear, an old form of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as a verb means to tear apart, and to lacerate is to tear flesh.

clue.text: Decide against revealing a personal view

indicators.note: the run of letters is shown within the words Decide against

explanation.surface: Choosing not to share one's own opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can mean an opinion or a view held by one person.

clue.text: Of South American extraction, gets very much heated

parts.note: Incan describes the South American people of Peru
extraction means ancestry or descent

explanation.surface: Someone of Latin American ancestry becomes furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing with heat, or figuratively in a fury, both strongly heated.

clue.text: District official is doubly confused in more vulgar surroundings

indicators.note: the more vulgar word forms the surroundings for the jumbled pair

parts.note: commoner is more common or coarse

indicators.note: confused says the doubled letters are scrambled
doubly says the word is taken twice

explanation.surface: A local official, twice muddled, mixes with a coarser crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'District' tempts as part of the wordplay but belongs to the definition; the word 'in' is only a link, with 'surroundings' doing the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A district commissioner was a colonial administrator in charge of a district.

clue.text: People must be mad to go off them

definitions.text: People must be mad to go off them

parts.words: People must be mad to go off them
parts.note: plays on the idiom going off one's head or one's carts, meaning crazy

explanation.walkthrough: Being off one's trolley is a British idiom for being mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off your carts in this idiom means crazy, so these are what mad people go off.

clue.text: Strangely pleads to cut out dead part of flower

indicators.note: strangely points to an odd rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for dead, as on genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone oddly pleads to cut out dead flower parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut out' removes D (dead) from PLEADS, and 'Strangely' shuffles what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like outer parts of a flower's calyx.

clue.text: Seasonal travellers are so damn stupid

indicators.note: stupid signals the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: An outburst at foolish travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads move with the seasons to find pasture, so seasonal travellers.

clue.text: Fool showing origin of Tarot card

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a card is a joker or wag, a witty person

explanation.surface: A fortune teller's opening tarot card shows the Fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fool is a real tarot card, which helps the surface; 'card' means a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly, foolish person, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Island beginning to show passion supporting volunteers

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit below the volunteers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: only the opening letter of show is taken

parts.note: a mania is a passionate obsession

explanation.surface: Volunteers start to show some passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an island state of Australia.

clue.text: Vehicle on which doctor pedals halfway

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: halfway takes the first half of the word pedals

explanation.surface: A doctor pedalling a bike only part of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits nicely: this vehicle has pedals as well as an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a light motorcycle with pedals, a vehicle.

clue.text: Politician — one embraced by church

indicators.note: embraced by puts the single figure inside the church

parts.note: a minster is a large church, like York Minster
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A politician welcomed by the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a government member heading a department, a politician.

clue.text: International leader fled country

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: fled means ran away

explanation.surface: An international head of state runs away from the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Water under the bridge means a loss for this transporter

definitions.text: Water under the bridge means a loss for this transporter

parts.words: Water under the bridge means a loss for this transporter
parts.note: the idiom for things past is read literally: a water-carrying bridge losing water through leaks

explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a bridge carrying a water channel; water escaping below would be a loss.

clue.text: Only man to lose a grave

parts.note: sole means only, as in sole survivor

indicators.note: to lose means the letter is taken away from the word man

explanation.surface: The only man to lose a grave plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a noun in the surface but is the adjective serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and solemn both mean serious and dignified.

clue.text: Have fun with egg plant

parts.note: to lark about is to have fun
to egg on is to spur, urge

explanation.surface: Messing about with eggs in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is the verb, as in egg on, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden plant, a delphinium.

clue.text: Engineers point to prompt delivery

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
S, south, is a point of the compass
a cue is a prompt, as given to an actor

explanation.surface: Engineers point to the need for prompt delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' means saving someone, being delivered from danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliverance from harm is a rescue, so delivery in that sense.

clue.text: Everything working fine in production of glossy metals

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of the letters

explanation.surface: A factory turns out shiny metals smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from rocket launches means every part is ready, so everything is working fine.

clue.text: Fellow in luck getting attic

indicators.note: the fellow goes inside the word for luck

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or luck

explanation.surface: A lucky fellow gets an attic room.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is the space under a roof, an attic.

clue.text: Language needing to be regularly repressed

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter of the word repressed

explanation.surface: A language that must be suppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Erse is a name for the Gaelic language, especially Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is Irish or Scottish Gaelic, a language.

clue.text: Common sense is almost useless

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the phrase for useless

parts.note: no use means useless

explanation.surface: Common sense is nearly worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is a British informal word for practical common sense.

clue.text: People who don't believe lies find trouble

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Lies cause trouble for unbelievers.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidels are unbelievers, those without the faith in question.

clue.text: Deplore amount charged by little administrator

parts.note: exec is a short form of executive, an administrator
a rate is a price or amount charged

explanation.surface: An executive's fee is deplorable.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or detest, so to deplore strongly.
